newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to higher in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"There was little impact on the market today despite another easing in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were quietly steady. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.88/0.83 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 0.85/0.80 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.57/1.52 percent against 1.55/1.50 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 was unchanged from Wednesday's close of S$98.99/99.04, September 2001 was unchanged at S$97.30/97.35 and June 2003 unchanged at S$95.30/95.35.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent versus Wednesday's 3 2-7/8 percent.
